findings.mechanism: BufferPool.free retains every returned buffer; the free list grows to the largest batch size (400 buffers) and is then reused
findings.cause: pool high-water mark, bounded by maxBatch=400 in workload.go
findings.evidence: Ran 6000 batches via a scratch test (removed afterwards), forcing GC every 1000: pool created=400/idle=400 from batch 1000 onward, HeapInuse 1960KB at 1000 batches and 2024KB at 6000 batches. Growth stops, and total retained is about 2MB.
findings.discriminator: The pool's created count stays flat at 400 and HeapInuse plateaus around 2MB across 6000 batches. The free list is bounded by the maximum batch size, and each Get pops a buffer that is later Put back, so there is no double-Put and no unbounded retention.

findings.mechanism: Renderer.index map holds rendered docs during a batch
findings.cause: index is emptied at the end of every RenderBatch (delete in the final loop)
findings.evidence: Code reading, plus the flat heap measurement above after 6000 batches.
findings.discriminator: Every entry is deleted at the end of RenderBatch, and invoice IDs are unique per batch, so the map is empty between batches.
